packages.label: אֲכִילָה יְתֵרָה וְהַכְּלִי
packages.reason: The central and only bechina identification in Torah #257 is the equation of eating beyond one's need (אכילה יתרה / אוכל יותר מצרכו) with placing food into a vessel (כלי). These two concepts share the same essential nature: both describe a state in which there is no living recipient to receive the food's vitality. A vessel cannot receive vitality — it is inert, it cannot use what is placed in it. Eating beyond need produces the same structural state: the extra food has no living root from which to receive vitality, since the person does not actually need it. The Rebbe states this equivalence twice: once descriptively ('הוא דומה כאילו הניחו האדם לתוך כלי') and once as the hermeneutic key to the verse ('הינו שלא תאכל יותר מצרכך, שזה דומה כנותן לתוך הכלי'). Polarity is 'neutral' because the keli is a structural/physical object used as a metaphor — it is not aligned with holiness or evil in this Torah; it is a neutral structural concept that describes the inert state of unclaimed food.
